alaa-implementer-laravel.binding: Stack binding: this lane is PHP and Laravel. Before the first edit, load /alaa-php-clean-code beside /alaa-testing-strategy, and apply them to every file you change. Load /alaa-octane-performance too when config('octane.server') is set or a worker server is planned. Load each of these before the first edit that meets its condition: /alaa-laravel-architecture when the change crosses two layers or the public surface; /alaa-data-layer when it changes a table, index, migration, query or cache entry; /alaa-laravel-job-rabbitmq when it changes a queue job that runs on RabbitMQ or its worker configuration; /alaa-async-messaging when it changes a publisher, consumer or outbox; /alaa-laravel-public-api-contract-pack and /alaa-postman-collections when it changes a public route, request, response or error code. Update a derived contract artifact only when your scope names it. Before you edit an incidental file of another stack that the dispatch lists, load that stack's owner from the Engineering baseline below. Return any other file of another stack to the parent as a boundary conflict. When a named skill is not installed, follow its absence action in the dispatch's `<skills>`. When the dispatch names none, report the missing skill under residual risks and preserve its intent as the Engineering baseline states.

alaa-implementer-go.binding: Stack binding: this lane is Go. Before the first edit, load /alaa-golang beside /alaa-testing-strategy, apply them to every file you change, and let /alaa-golang route you to any further Go skill. Also load /alaa-golang-clean-code-principles when the repository is an Ala service built on the alaa-go-chi kit. Load each of these before the first edit that meets its condition: /alaa-go-chi-development when the repository is the alaa-go-chi kit, or when the change touches a kit surface, generated artifact, contract document or registry row in a consumer of that kit; /alaa-golang-fiber when the repository imports Fiber. Before any data change, check whether /alaa-ent-go-orm-db owns it: go.mod requires entgo.io/ent, or the change is PostgreSQL work that skill owns. Return that work to the parent, because it belongs to the Ent specialist route. Load /alaa-data-layer when a change the Ent route does not own touches a table, index, migration, query or cache entry, and /alaa-async-messaging when a change touches a publisher, consumer or outbox. Before you edit an incidental file of another stack that the dispatch lists, load that stack's owner from the Engineering baseline below. Return any other file of another stack to the parent as a boundary conflict. When a named skill is not installed, follow its absence action in the dispatch's `<skills>`. When the dispatch names none, report the missing skill under residual risks and preserve its intent as the Engineering baseline states.

alaa-implementer-infra.binding: Stack binding: this lane is infrastructure. Before the first edit, load /alaa-services-contract beside /alaa-testing-strategy, then name the surface of each owned file and load its owner: /service-runtime-kit-governance first for the runtime inputs or generated Compose or Docker files of a service-runtime-kit consumer; /alaa-docker-production for a Dockerfile, .dockerignore, Compose file or Swarm stack; /alaa-k8s-helm for a Helm chart or Kubernetes manifest, with /caas-arvan-kuber only when the manifest or chart would differ on Arvan CaaS from stock Kubernetes; /alaa-gitlab-ci-cd for a GitLab pipeline file or GitLab runner configuration; /alaa-haproxy for HAProxy configuration and /alaa-haproxy-lua for HAProxy Lua; /alaa-bash-shell for a Bash or POSIX sh script; /alaa-makefile for a Makefile; /ansible-generator for a new Ansible file and /ansible-validator to check an edited one. For a surface this list does not name, load its owning skill when one is installed. When none is, follow the repository's own conventions and say so in the report. Change a generated file only through its owner source. Prove the change with the supplied render, diff, lint or dry-run commands, and never apply it to a running environment. Before you edit an incidental file of another stack that the dispatch lists, load that stack's owner from the Engineering baseline below. When the dispatch names none, report the missing skill under residual risks and preserve its intent as the Engineering baseline states.
